newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish beet planting starting up in early April.
newsitem.headline: Danish beet planting starting up in early April.

text.p: Sugar beet sowing will start in Denmark in early April, Danish packaging, food and sugar producer Danisco said on Wednesday.
"We are starting up sugar beet sowing in Denmark these days and intend to continue if the present weather persists," a Danisco spokesman told Reuters.

He said Denmark's most intense sugar beet plantings took place in the southern islands of Lolland and Falster, with more scattered cultivation in Zealand, the central island of Funen and east Jutland.
In Sweden, planting takes place mainly in the south.
The spokesman said it would be not be possible to give a realistic idea of sowing campaign progress until end-April.
He was unable to comment on the sowing situation in Danisco's plantations in Sweden and Germany.
Danisco, Europe's fourth biggest sugar producer, has a virtual monopoly of sugar production in Denmark and Sweden, with areas also in eastern Germany.
